Subject: Skyline Health — streaming & concurrency SLO validation checkpoints

Alex — thanks for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed checkpoints so we can align on the SLO acceptance criteria before procurement engages. Short version up top: we recommend a staged validation approach (smoke -> scale -> production-canary) with clear pass/fail thresholds for latency, concurrency, and streaming continuity.

Key items we agreed on during the call:
- Target p95/p99 latency for single-turn responses: p95 < 60ms, p99 < 180ms at 99th percentile of normal traffic patterns.
- Streaming continuity: first-byte < 50ms for streamed responses; token arrival cadence no more than 75ms between tokens for streaming UX.
- Concurrency/throughput baseline: Sustained 500 concurrent streams for pilot; scale target 2,000 concurrent streams for production. Equivalent throughput target ~12k tokens/sec aggregate (estimate).
- Fallback behavior: auto-fallback to a 7B quantized variant when CPU/GPU contention > 85% on the pool; must preserve final quality checks.

Proposed validation checkpoints (deliverables & owners):
1) Smoke run (week of Aug 24) — confirm endpoints, auth, and one end-to-end streamed conversation. Owner: Monica. Deliverable: recording + checklist.
2) Load validation (Aug 26–28) — synthetic load to 1.5x pilot concurrency (750 concurrent). Owner: Rishi. Deliverable: load-test report + dashboard links.
3) Production canary (Sep 2–4) — short A/B canary under real traffic with SLA monitoring. Owner: Skyline (ops) + Redwood on watch. Deliverable: canary runbook + rollback plan.

Decision criteria to advance from load validation to canary (must pass all):
- p99 latency <= 180ms under the target concurrency profile.
- Streaming continuity shows <2% session-level stream interruptions.
- CPU/GPU utilization stable with headroom >= 15%.
- No >5% increase in tokenized cost after applying suggested batching and prefix caching (we'll provide exact numbers).

Attachments: I uploaded the demo recording and a sample SLO checklist to the shared Drive (links below).

Next steps: Can you confirm the procurement contact and whether the pilot will be run in us-east-1? If yes, we'll schedule the smoke run for Mon Aug 24 at 10am PT.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Monica — adding a few technical clarifications and proposed test knobs so Skyline's infra team can reproduce results: 

Test configuration suggestions (to include in the load validation):
- Model variant: rdx-13b-v2 (float16) for pilot. Quantized 7B fallback: rdx-7b-q4f16.
- Sequence lengths: run three profiles — short (20 tokens), median (120 tokens), long (512 tokens). We'll weight the synthetic load 60/30/10 respectively.
- Warm KV cache step: 5k synthetic prefixes for streaming warmup to approximate real-world cache hit rates.
- Batching: continuous batching window 25ms; target request coalescing to batch sizes of 8–16 for throughput runs.
- Observability: enable token-level latency traces and gRPC streaming metrics; we'll provide a Prometheus scrape job and Grafana dashboard link.

I'll attach a quick load-test summary from a comparable pilot we ran last quarter so Alex can see the format. If Skyline's infra wants different knobs (e.g., different batching window), we can adjust.

Deliverables I'm producing before the smoke run:
- load-test-summary-20260821.pdf (high-level results + config)
- adjusted slo-validation-checklist.xlsx (includes exact pass/fail thresholds and test commands)

Rishi
